about: On Holy Thursday this part of the Canon recalls the most sacred day on which Christ was handed over for us, then commemorates Mary, Joseph and the saints. The priest says it quietly as part of the continuing prayer addressed to the Father.

s01.translation: Remaining in communion and celebrating the most sacred day on which our Lord

s03.translation: Jesus Christ was handed over for us,

s04.translation: we also venerate the memory, first of all, of the glorious ever-Virgin

s06.translation: Mary, Mother of that same God and our Lord

alignments.gloss: Mother of that same God and our Lord

s09.translation: and also of blessed Joseph, Spouse of that same Virgin,

s10.translation: and Your blessed Apostles and Martyrs: Peter and Paul, Andrew, James, John, Thomas, James, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Simon and Thaddeus,

s11.translation: Linus, Cletus, Clement, Sixtus, Cornelius, Cyprian, Lawrence, Chrysogonus, John and Paul, Cosmas and Damian

s12.translation: and all Your saints. Through their merits and prayers, grant that in everything we may be strengthened by the aid of Your protection.

alignments.gloss: we may be strengthened by the aid of Your protection

s14.translation: Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

w001.explanation: The communion belongs to those praying within the continuing Canon. The celebration of the day and veneration of the saints’ memory belong to that same praying “we”.

w005.explanation: The day is identified by Christ’s being handed over for us. Its celebration joins the Holy Thursday commemoration to His Passion.

w018.explanation: The veneration of memory includes Mary, Joseph and the following list of saints. The prayer remains addressed to the Father.

w026.explanation: “That same” points back to Jesus Christ, handed over for us. Mary is named as the Mother of that same Christ, called God and Lord.

w037.explanation: “That same Virgin” refers to Mary. Joseph is named as her spouse.
